# XrealXRInputRouter

**Inherits:** [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)  
**Script:** `addons/godot_xreal/xr_input_router.gd`  

Runtime-neutral bridge between Godot XR controller trackers and InputMap actions.

An OpenXR runtime provides the `left_hand` and `right_hand` trackers itself. On XREAL this router creates trackers under those same reserved names and polls the native phone controller, so the scene and its gameplay code read one contract on either platform.

## Properties

<a id="property-bias_learn"></a>

### bias_learn: float = 0.02

Rate used to learn the resting gyroscope bias.

<a id="property-gravity_gain"></a>

### gravity_gain: float = 0.06

Complementary-filter gain used to correct phone pitch and roll from gravity.

<a id="property-gyro_deadzone"></a>

### gyro_deadzone: float = 0.012

Gyroscope rates below this threshold are treated as resting noise.

<a id="property-hand_offset"></a>

### hand_offset: Vector3 = Vector3(0.28, -0.32, -0.3)

Phone-controller origin relative to the tracked head, in metres. Negative Y puts the origin below the head, at hand height. X is a magnitude; set_active_hand picks its sign.

<a id="property-left_controller"></a>

### left_controller: XRController3D

Optional explicit wiring. Left empty, bind_controllers() picks the XRController3D nodes under the origin by their tracker name, so an application may name and nest its own however it likes.

<a id="property-right_controller"></a>

### right_controller: XRController3D


## Methods

<a id="method-bind_controllers"></a>

### bind_controllers(origin: Node)

Adopt the application's controller nodes. Matching on `tracker` rather than on node names keeps this working whether they are called LeftHand, LeftAim or LeftController, and an application that separates aim and grip poses simply has more than one node per hand; the first of each wins.

<a id="method-enable_xreal_trackers"></a>

### enable_xreal_trackers(system: Object = null)

Create the standard controller trackers only for the XREAL backend. OpenXR owns its trackers. When supplied, XrealSystem is polled here for the native phone controller.

<a id="method-get_active_controller"></a>

### get_active_controller() -> XRController3D

Standard controller node currently representing the XREAL phone controller.

<a id="method-get_phone_controller_pose"></a>

### get_phone_controller_pose() -> Transform3D

Current synthetic phone-controller pose in tracking space.

<a id="method-has_phone_controller_pose"></a>

### has_phone_controller_pose() -> bool

Whether the native phone controller has produced a recentered pose.

<a id="method-poll_xreal_controller"></a>

### poll_xreal_controller(delta: float, head_transform: Transform3D)

Poll and publish the native XREAL phone controller. Call after head tracking becomes live.

<a id="method-pulse_button"></a>

### pulse_button(input_name: StringName)

Emit a canonical button pulse for controls that report clicks rather than down/up.

The press is held across two process_frame signals, not one. A click arriving from the glasses callback is published during the backend driver's _process, so a node that processes earlier in the tree has already run for that frame; releasing on the first process_frame would retract the action before any such node could poll it. Two frames leave every node exactly one _process in which is_action_pressed() reads true. Because the press starts mid-process rather than in the input phase, is_action_just_pressed() is NOT reliable for these clicks: connect to XRController3D.button_pressed, or poll is_action_pressed(). Clicks can also arrive faster than one pulse takes. A tracker input only signals on change, so re-raising a button that is still held would publish nothing at all; the button is dropped first so the second click reads as its own press. The generation counter then keeps the older pulse from releasing partway through the newer one.

<a id="method-recenter_phone_controller"></a>

### recenter_phone_controller()

Make the current native phone orientation point forward.
